children.title: 📄 Climbing the Hill: Prompt Injection Red-Teaming Against Frontier Models with Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
children.description: Yin et al., 2026. Addresses the cold-start problem in RL-based prompt-injection red-teaming (every attempt against a frontier model fails, yielding zero reward) by training the attacker LLM against a curriculum of increasingly robust targets, each warm-started from the last; reaches ASR@10 of 93.8% and 45.0% against two frontier models where prior RL methods score 0%, and the trained attacker transfers to six other frontier models it never attacked. Code.

repo_info.description: PIForge: An Open Framework for RL-based Prompt Injection Red Teaming.

children.title: 📄 Piggybacking on Perception: Stealthy Concurrent Audio Prompt Injections against Multimodal LLM Agents
children.description: Liu et al., 2026. Hides malicious audio instructions that imperceptibly "piggyback" onto user speech to hijack continuous-audio multimodal agents (69.1% attack success against Gemini 3 Pro), introducing the AudioAgentSecurity benchmark (8 scenarios, 10 attack patterns) and a Cascaded Audio Decoupling and Verification (CADV) defense that reaches over 90% detection via acoustic source separation and cross-modal consistency. Code.

children.title: 📄 Control-Token Injection Suppresses Chain-of-Thought and Defeats Reasoning-Based Oversight in Tool-Using Agents
children.description: Usama et al., 2026. Shows agent safety is a joint property of the model and its decoding harness: appending a single string of the model's own channel-control tokens makes the tokenizer render an already-complete reasoning turn, so the model emits zero chain-of-thought (52.5→0 tokens) yet still fires the tool call every trial, converting 39.6% of refusals into completed exfiltrations and blinding reasoning-based monitors; separately shows whether an identical tool call fires is decided by the harness parser, not the model. Code

repo_info.description: Experiments for control-token chain-of-thought suppression and parser-leniency attacks on tool-using LLM agents

children.title: 📄 Scanning the Harness: An Empirical Study of Supply-Chain Defects in AI Coding-Agent Configurations
children.description: Kapner et al., 2026. Studies the AI coding-agent harness (instruction files, skills, hooks, MCP declarations, subagents) as an unlocked dependency layer across 3,171 public GitHub repositories, validating every finding via independent re-derivation, an LLM adjudicator, and a second re-check; confirms three security classes — 9.8% of setups pin no MCP server version, 3.1% pre-approve arbitrary execution behind scoped-looking grants (e.g. ), and 3.8% carry a skill that pre-approves the shell for whoever installs it (shipping inside 3.7% of published collections) — with 16.0% of setups carrying a security defect. Tool

repo_info.description: Evaluate (lint, review, and security-audit) your AI coding agent harness.

children.title: 📄 SkillPoison: Progressive Skill Poisoning via Successful Experiences
children.description: Zhang et al., 2026. Shows skill poisoning can arise from verified successful experiences without any individual trajectory being malicious: SkillPoison constructs a set of successful experiences reinforcing a target behavior, then removes the contextual conditions that constrain when it applies, shaping how the skill extractor generalizes so useful behavior supports task success while harmful behavior emerges when misapplied — reaching 95.71% attack success across three benchmarks with every injected experience remaining task-correct and passing verification and lexical inspection. Code

children.title: 📄 A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
children.description: Li et al., AACL-IJCNLP 2026. Two-stage black-box framework hijacking MCP agents via a semantic supply-chain vector: an Attraction phase optimizes attacker tool metadata to raise invocation probability, then a Manipulation phase uses execution traces to refine adversarial tool returns; on LiveMCPBench it reaches a 93.6% malicious-tool invocation rate and 74.4% mean attack success across exfiltration, integrity-compromise, and reasoning-derailment scenarios, transferring to four other models without re-optimization. Code

children.title: 📄 ChatInject: Abusing Chat Templates for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
children.description: Chang et al., ICLR 2026. Formats injected payloads to mimic native chat templates (optionally primed by persuasive multi-turn dialogue) so agents elevate them to system-level trust; transfers across models and largely bypasses prompt-based defenses. Code.

repo_info.description: [ICLR 2026] Official implementation of "ChatInject: Abusing Chat Templates for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents"

children.title: 📄 StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
children.description: Zhan et al., 2026. Introduces multi-step indirect prompt injection, decomposing an adversarial goal into innocuous-looking sub-steps distributed across a chain of pages along the agent's navigation path; the resulting 480-example StepJack benchmark raises attack success on computer-use agents by up to 31.2 points at fixed decomposition depth (e.g., GPT-5.4-mini 41.7%→72.9%). Code.

children.title: 📄 ActGuard: Pre-execution Action Auditing against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
children.description: Wang et al., 2026. Rather than judging whether external content is suspicious, ActGuard predicts a local tool prior for each upcoming action and, before execution, compares the candidate action against it via tool-level contrastive analysis and parameter-level evidence localization, masking only spans confirmed malicious and regenerating the action — preserving planning flexibility while cutting attack success to state-of-the-art levels at near no-attack utility. Code.

children.title: 📄 Understanding and Enhancing Backdoor Persistency in LLM Agent Post-Training
children.description: Zhan et al., EMNLP 2026 Findings. Studies a supply-chain threat where a third-party base model carries a backdoor and asks whether it survives a developer's benign supervised fine-tuning and subsequent task-level RL; finds benign SFT substantially reduces attack success but subsequent RL often preserves or even increases it, identifies initial backdoor strength and gradient compatibility as survival factors, and proposes PersistBD to deliberately refine an already-backdoored model before release — raising attack success on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B from 20% to 74% after SFT and 76% after SFT-RL while maintaining benign task performance. Code

children.title: 📄 Janus: A Playground for User-Involved Agentic Permission Management
children.description: Brigham et al., 2026. Playground system implementing six permission assistants across a design space of user involvement in agentic tool-call authorization; shows user input meaningfully strengthens privacy and security, AI augmentation of user decisions reduces cognitive load, and permission fatigue must be modeled since no single design is optimal across contexts. Code.

children.title: 📄 A Safety-Bounded SDC-to-MCP Gateway for Medical AI Agents
children.description: Gerlach & Fischer, 2026. IEEE 11073 SDC-to-MCP gateway that exposes device metrics, alarms, and semantic metadata as read-only resources while representing selected action affordances only as policy-validated dry-run tools, enforcing a narrow no-execution property (agent-facing requests dispatch no device operation); a Python/Java prototype preserves the no-execution boundary across resource, proposal, and authorization paths under simulated fault and lifecycle experiments. Code

children.title: 📄 Beyond Handcrafted Security: Self-Evolving Defense (SED) for LLM Agents
children.description: 2026. Training-free framework that distills harmful agent trajectories into reusable security policies without updating model weights, retrieving relevant policies for future tasks to continually adapt across jailbreaks, prompt injection, and insecure code generation; lowers targeted prompt-injection success on AgentDojo to 0.42% (vs. 3.7% best baseline) and holds adaptive X-Teaming attack success on HarmBench to 7.8% across three open-source models. Code.

children.title: 📄 ZoneClaw: Mitigating Persistent Memory Attacks by Establishing Memory-Zoning in OpenClaw-Style Computer-Use Agents
children.description: Ma et al., 2026. Targets the persistent memory attack where reloaded workspace memory lets an attacker who controls only benign-looking external content induce a CUA to record attacker-favored claims during a legitimate task that then govern later untouched tasks ("malicious context → memory injection → malicious execution"); ZoneClaw replaces flat workspace memory with hierarchical trust zones where external claims persist in a low-trust zone and gain action-guiding authority only by crossing an explicit boundary cross-checked against unwritable zones, enforced by asymmetric-privilege processes so no process both ingests external content and acts outward — driving ASR from 372/480 to 6/480 while retaining utility in 458/480 trials. Code.

children.title: 📄 HARDE: Optimizing Agent Harnesses for Runtime Risk Detection and Execution Control
children.description: Liu et al., 2026. Risk-aware harness that structures LLM-based monitoring into trigger, monitor, and feedback modules for targeted safety interventions during execution, plus a two-stage optimization framework that first probes each module in isolation to derive an optimization guide, then iteratively tunes the harness against safety and utility feedback; across three attack benchmarks it improves runtime safety while preserving benign utility, outperforming manually designed harnesses and naive optimization baselines. Code

repo_info.description: Code release for HARDE: Optimizing Agent Harnesses for Runtime Risk Detection and Execution Control.

children.title: 📄 Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Intent-Reasoning-Action Auditing for Autonomous Coding Agents
children.description: Ghosh, 2026. Dependency-free auditing system that captures three channels per coding-agent session (human intent, model self-report, executed actions) into a hash-chained, externally anchorable ledger, gating tool calls with a pre-execution policy and re-verifying the ledger live; across 1,600 mutations the chain detects every edit while a regex gate blocks only 41% of harmful tool calls, and in 14 real Claude Code runs the agent never acted on four planted indirect prompt injections. Code.

repo_info.description: Tamper-evident tracing, policy gates and cross-checks for AI coding agents: see what the agent did, and why.

children.title: 📄 Tool Specifications Matter: Uncovering and Mitigating Safety Risks in AI Agents
children.description: Pan et al., 2026. Identifies schema-formatted tool specifications as a primary source of agent safety degradation — white-box representation analysis shows they weaken the model's internal refusal signals — and proposes SafeKeep, an inference-time safeguard that judges requests against flattened textual tool specs while executing with the original schema, raising harmful-request refusal from 23.8% to 70.6% and cutting observation-level prompt-injection success from 25.6% to 2.5%. Code.

repo_info.description: Tool Specifications Matter: Uncovering and Mitigating Safety Risks in AI Agents

children.title: 📄 Certified Multi-Source Integrity for Structured Agent Actions
children.description: Pandey et al., UKAI 2026. Characterizes when a policy-bound structured agent action (e.g., paying an invoice) assembled from corruptible documents and tool outputs is safely certifiable under a corruption budget, and gives the maximally live safe certifier — admitting an action only when each field clears a bounded corruption radius over corruption-distinct evidence classes counted by a minimum hitting set; across five models in a real agent loop a realistic injection fools all but one while the certifier admits no unsafe action and recovers correct values where corroboration permits. Code.

children.title: 📄 Universal Defenses for Tool-Integrated LLM Agents Against Adversarial Attacks
children.description: Li & Wang, 2026. Explores generalizable defenses spanning four attack types at once (direct/indirect prompt injection, memory poisoning, backdoor) via two universal tool-based mechanisms — Attacker Tool Filtering, which uses anomaly detection (e.g. Isolation Forest) to remove suspicious tools, and Normal Tool Recalling, a white-box method restoring the agent's original toolset before planning — plus chain-of-thought, self-reflection, and task-paraphrasing prompt defenses; across four open-source and three proprietary LLMs (through GPT-5) it reaches 0% attack success in many settings while preserving task success. Code

children.title: 📄 Passing the Test You Trained On: Re-evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors for LLM Agents
children.description: Liu, 2026. Replays ground-truth tool calls of AgentDojo and tau-bench without an LLM to obtain benign-by-construction tool outputs, labels injections by differential replay, and evaluates fifteen detectors (including Meta's Prompt Guard 2) plus two task-aware judges; detection rankings transfer poorly across benchmarks (the BIPIA leader catches 2% of AgentDojo injections at 1% FPR), arguing deployment evaluations must use the agent's own tool outputs, report detection at a low false-positive rate, and audit the detector's training data. Code.

repo_info.description: Re-evaluating prompt-injection detectors on LLM agent tool outputs (paper draft, scripts, scores)

children.title: 📄 Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
children.description: Wang et al., 2026. PIMiner, an agentic prompt-injection red-teaming system that builds a transferable strategy library from scratch during training and applies it to previously unseen target LLMs without retraining using only ~10 queries per sample, reaching up to 86.7% ASR on AgentDojo and 76.2% on IPIArena against frontier models. Code.

children.title: 📄 Red-Teaming Auto Mode: Improving Blocking Classifiers Against Malign Coding Agents
children.description: Remedios et al., 2026. Red-teams production blocking monitors that review each proposed coding-agent action before it runs (Auto Mode in Claude Code, Guardian in OpenAI's Codex) under a persistently-misaligned agent rather than only untrusted-source injections; adversarial agents given high-level strategies evade monitors via agent-generated prompt injection, multi-agent attacks, and malicious compaction — running arbitrary bash in 79% of trials — and the paper shows design changes (broader tool coverage, transcript formatting, an agentic monitor stage) that harden Auto Mode while leaving multi-context attacks an open problem. Code.

children.title: 📄 Ajar: Measuring Open Privilege in Agent Defenses
children.description: Sharma et al., 2026. Introduces a third evaluation axis beyond attack success and benign utility: open privilege — the unneeded transfers, deletions, or broad reads a defense still permits on benign tasks — attaching to AgentDojo and exposing that Progent, CaMeL, AC4A, Permission Assistant, and Claude Code's Auto mode leave widely different amounts of privilege open (code).

repo_info.description: Measuring Open Privilege in Agent Defenses

items.title: Ziran
items.description: Security testing framework for AI agents that models tools as a graph to find dangerous tool chains, execution-level side effects, and multi-phase exploits

items.title: node9
items.description: Security and governance layer that checks every tool call from coding agents and MCP servers before it runs: credential jail, secret and PII detection, human approval for risky actions, MCP tool definition pinning, SHA-256 pinning of installed skills and plugins, and one audit record across agents

repo_info.description: Access control for AI agents. Set what Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and any MCP server are allowed to do, review risky actions before they run, and keep every action on the record.

items.title: Vestige
items.description: Local safety and memory layer for AI agents: Operator Lite, a hook-based gate whose deterministic rules block destructive agent shell commands (force-push, destructive SQL, reverse shells, cloud-metadata access) before they run, and Strata, an append-only hash-chained memory log that traces poisoned memory back to the write that introduced it

repo_info.description: Local deterministic memory and safety kernel for AI agents. Replaces vector RAG with STRATA, a cryptographically signed, append-only ledger, so every agent state carries proof.  Uses causal_walk engine to trace execution failures back to their root cause, and Operator Lite to block destructive terminal terminal commands before they ever run
